title: Opposition stages walkout in Kerala Assembly over alleged police atrocities

tea.why: Protesting alleged police atrocities, lapses in investigations, and a dual justice system for the wealthy.
tea.want: A formal discussion on recurring police excesses and accountability in recent high-profile cases.
tea.changed: Oct 27, 2026: The Opposition walked out of the Kerala Assembly after the Speaker rejected an adjournment motion.

summary: In Thiruvananthapuram, the Opposition staged a walkout in the Kerala Legislative Assembly after the Speaker denied an adjournment motion seeking a discussion on alleged police atrocities and lapses. Led in the motion by MLA A.C. Moideen, the Opposition accused the government of running a dual justice system that favors the wealthy and influential. They cited multiple incidents, including a fatal car crash in Cheranalloor involving a judge's minor son and a fatal collision near the Kochi airport, alleging police mishandling, failure to apply appropriate culpable homicide charges, and undue influence. Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala responded that the government takes the incidents seriously, would not protect anyone regardless of position, and had directed senior officials to probe lapses and support the victim's family.
demands: Conduct a legislative discussion on police atrocities
Ensure accountability in high-profile accident cases involving minors and influential persons
Address alleged custodial violence and assaults on civilians and students
response: Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala stated the government took the Cheranalloor incident seriously, would not shield wrongdoers regardless of position, and had ordered senior officials to investigate lapses.

updates.text: The Opposition moved an adjournment motion in the Kerala Assembly to discuss alleged police atrocities and a dual justice system.
The Speaker denied permission for the motion following a response from the Home Minister, prompting the Opposition to stage a walkout.
